items.text: AMEND AND RECOMMIT TO ENERGY AND TELECOMMUNICATIONS

items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the public service law, in relation to net energy metering for
fuel-flexible linear generator electric generating equipment
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S8327

SPONSOR: KENNEDY
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the public service law, in relation to net energy meter-
ing for fuel-flexible linear generator electric generating equipment

 
PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:

This bill would provide parity in "net energy metering" for fuel-flexi-
ble linear generators under Public Service Law § 66-j.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Sections 1 through 12: Amends the public service law to to provide pari-
ty in net energy metering for fuel-flexible linear generator electric
generating equipment.

Section 13: Is the effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

In 2019, the New York legislature passed historic climate legislation
aimed at reducing greenhouse gas emissions economy-wide, but especially
from the burning of fossil fuels in the electric generation sector. In
recent years, New York has also focused on bolstering resiliency and
ensuring the push towards a clean energy future includes an electricity
system capable of withstanding extreme weather events and other poten-
tially disruptive events. Because the availability of reliable, resil-
ient, and affordable electric service is critical to the welfare of
citizenry and is central to New York's economy", the State has aggres-
sively pursued a strategy known as "Reforming the Energy Vision" (REV),
through which "New York is actively spurring clean energy innova-
tion...promoting more efficient use of energy, deeper penetration of
renewable energy resources such as wind and solar, and wider deployment
of 'distributed' energy resources, such as micro grids, 'roof-top solar
and other on-site power supplies...." (1) The success of REV will depend
in part upon the right mix of clean energy technologies being available
in order for New York to achieve its ambitious energy goals and this
includes the critical need for distributed energy resources (DERs) that
are clean, fully dispatchable (2), and available for the duration of
potentially prolonged (i.e., multi-day) grid outages.  Distributed ener-
gy resources contribute to a more robust electric grid, lower costs for
users, and lower greenhouse gas emissions by offering: (i) a reliable,
resilient power source during outages, running independently from the
grid, (ii) flexible usage to offset energy consumption from the central
grid during peak hours and compensate for renewable energy sources
during non-available hours, (iii) low-emissions energy using a variety
of fuel sources, and (iv) reduced power grid infrastructure.costs and
losses.

One such technology is the fuel-flexible linear generator which,
although bearing several similarities to fuel cells, represents an
entirely new category of power generation. Linear generator technology
uses a novel electromechanical process by which a low-temperature
reaction of air and fuel drives magnets through copper coils to produce
electricity at very' high efficiencies but with near-zero NOx emissions.
Linear generators can run on clean and environmentally friendly fuels,
such as hydrogen and renewable biogas, but also seamlessly transition to
other available fuels if other circumstances require it.

While current law recognizes a wide variety of DERs, including fuel
cells and several other fuel-based technologies, the Public Service Law
does not encompass cutting-edge linear generator technology. This bill
would amend the Public Service Law to cover fuel-flexible linear genera-
tor technology for net metering purposes, allowing customers to benefit
from this promising new source of affordable, clean and fully dispatcha-
ble on-site power generation. Indeed, providing parity for linear gener-
ators will help ensure a more stable, secure, and environmentally
responsible electric grid, and bring New York's ambitious clean energy
and resiliency goals within closer reach.  Public Service Law section
66-j is the basis for many other dean energy policies and other technol-
ogies are on list already. The addition of linear generators creates
parity and ensures comparable and equitable regulatory treatment if, and
only if, future policies leverage this comprehensive list. New York has
previously provided parity-recognition for this technology when it added
fuel-flexible linear generators to the list of technologies eligible for
sales tax relief (FY-2017-18 Budget), and most recently, property tax
relief pursuant to Chapter 325 of the Laws of 2018.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

energy and telecommunications A10268 05/04/20 amend and recommit to
energy A10268 05/04/20 print number 10268a

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS FOR STATE AND LOCAL GOVERNMENTS:

None.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
Immediately.

(2) Dispatchable generation refers to sources of electricity that can be
used on demand, according to market needs, with or without the grid.
Dispatchable generators can adjust their power output according to need,
turn off and on quickly, and provide backup power when the grid is down.
